terms.gloss: a summary of one’s education and career
terms.grammar: phrase: curriculum, curriculī n., with the genitive vītae
evidence: M-O s.v. curriculum vitae, c.v., résumé
terms.comment: Classical words: Cicero speaks of the short course of life, exiguum vītae curriculum (Rab. Perd. 30, in Lewis & Short). Morgan–Owens records the phrase in Latin for an account of one’s education and career since the early nineteenth century; English took it from Latin.

phrases.latin: exiguum nōbīs vītae curriculum nātūra circumscrīpsit
phrases.english: nature has marked out a short course of life for us

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. curriculum vitae, c.v., résumé.
